thread:
priya: quick heads-up — ran a microbatch bringup for the new tiny-embed variant with int6 quant + prefix cache disabled and saw recall@3 drop ~6% on short/noisy queries. attaching quick notes below.
ben: ouch. short/noisy = examples?
priya: samples: 
- "how to reset password?"
- "best cheap headphones 2026"
- "why my email bounced"
these are short, conversational, sometimes truncated.
lucy: do we have a baseline for the same samples with the float model (no quant)?
priya: baseline recall@3 (float32) = 0.78, int6 microbatch run = 0.72. k=1 drop small, k=3 bigger.
sam: can you paste the run config/command?
priya: ran with: ```./run_onboard.sh --model tiny-v2 --quant int6 --microbatch 4 --kvcache disabled --seed 42```
kate: microbatch 4 + kvcache off could increase index scatter for short prefixes. try microbatch 1 or enable prefix caching to see delta.
ben: also try per-channel calibration (per-channel quant) — sometimes fixes short-query tails.
priya: good call. will try per-channel and microbatch=1 tonight.
ci-bot: summary: 1753456789 - onboard-run - tiny-v2 int6 - recall@3 0.72 - tests 1200 q
lucy: another angle — check nearest-neighbor distance distributions for anchors vs float. maybe centroid shift after quant.
sam: if centroid shift is real, consider small re-embedding of anchor set with quantized model (cheap) or fallback to float for low-confidence queries.
priya: I ran a quick histogram of cosine diffs this morning; shifting mass ~0.02 mean decrease for short queries. uploading plot to #eng-ml-reports.
kate: can we add a small canary route: if top1 score < 0.25, fallback to float endpoint? we should simulate cost impact first.
ben: cool — also log cases where anchor identity flips (id change) between float and quant for the same query. that'll help prioritize.
priya: will collect idflip list tomorrow and share.
ci-bot: test triggered: 1753456789-perf-scan (will post results when done) :gear:
sam: thanks — low-effort triage plan: 1) microbatch=1 vs 4, 2) per-channel quant, 3) kvcache on/off, 4) idflip heatmap. priya pls run 1-3, lucy take 4.
priya: on it. tagging @kate for canary fallback design when we have numbers. :thumbsup:
kate: ack. will draft fallback cost sim later today.
priya: quick note — if anyone has other short-query sample sets (support logs, search logs) please DM. want broader coverage than the 1.2k test set.
ben: I have a small support-derived set of ~600 queries, pushing to your gdrive.
priya: perfect, thanks. I'll rerun with those tomorrow and report back.
lucy: thanks team. low-churn thread but important — catching this early avoids rollout regressions. :eyes:
